reason: Chest pain presumed cardiac distress and emergency treatment given in transport; origin was residence after earlier discharge, so inpatient exclusion does not apply.
Multiple therapy disciplines, measurable improvement and intensive therapy asserted with PT/OT daily; two agents support and the documentation concern is not decisive.
Oral meds and caregiver-given insulin are not skilled care, stability at discharge, and illegible/stamped physician signatures undermine the plan of care.
Coumadin dosage was being adjusted with out-of-range INR, so nurse prothrombin monitoring and skilled observation were reasonable and necessary under a plan of care.
Beneficiary was stable with normal vitals, no treatment given during transport, and no necessity shown for ambulance.
Appellant conceded ground transport was reasonable, vitals were stable, and a closer capable facility existed, so air ambulance necessity is not shown.
Record does not show what service the sending hospital (also a trauma center) lacked, so the receiving hospital is not shown to be the nearest appropriate facility.
Non-emergency transport; reason for oxygen unexplained, patient could walk, and the rehabilitation-center destination is not shown to be a qualifying hospital/CAH/SNF.
IRF admission with daily PT and OT, multiple disciplines, and measurable functional improvement support coverage; unresolved documentation points are not shown to defeat it.
Inpatient decision was recorded as an error and reverted to observation; observation orders do not meet inpatient admission requirements.
Destination was a physician-staffed urgent care clinic, and ambulance service to a physician-directed clinic is not covered.
Infrequent adult day care/medical absences do not defeat homebound status, functional limitations are documented, and unstable blood sugars with medication changes justify skilled observation.
Chest pain with new T-wave inversion, extensive cardiac history and catheterization with stenting support a hospital inpatient stay; nothing in the facts contradicts the inpatient admission.
Transfer for cardiology was needed, but payment is limited to the 133 miles to the nearer appropriate hospital; the other 70 miles are not covered.
Skilled speech-language/dysphagia therapy was physician-ordered, improvement was documented, and coverage does not depend solely on improvement potential.
Long-standing stable pattern, no medication/plan changes, unassessed edema and no skilled teaching documented, so skilled observation is not justified.
No physician certification of homebound status, and the beneficiary leaves home four days weekly independently with no showing the day-care center is licensed or accredited.
Pouring a mediplanner and overseeing aides is not skilled, no change in condition was documented, and aide hours exceed the part-time limit.
Hospitalization was documented as due to extensive dissection and significant pulmonary disease with oxygen and assessments; nothing in the record shows the stay was not warranted.
Nurses assessed, dressed and taught wound care for pressure ulcer and other wounds in a diabetic patient, which is skilled nursing care.
Family could safely perform the care, diabetes was controlled orally, and plan of care/oral order signature requirements were not met.
Skilled gait training was physician-ordered, performed each visit, and documented improvement in fall-risk score.
